maker: John Kemeny and Thomas Kurtz, Dartmouth College
summary: Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code, made at Dartmouth so every student could program. Microsoft's version for the Altair started the company, and BASIC came built into almost every home computer of the late 1970s and 1980s.

events.note: The first BASIC programs run on Dartmouth’s time-sharing system.

events.label: Altair BASIC
events.note: Microsoft’s first product, a BASIC for the Altair 8800.

events.label: Home computers
events.note: The TRS-80, Commodore PET and Apple II ship with BASIC built in.

events.label: Visual Basic
events.note: Microsoft pairs BASIC with a visual form designer.
